citations.claim: energy rises after one large dt step

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.03119 to 0.005 (single field); smaller timestep makes integration accurate so energy no longer exceeds bound

explanation: With no walls or controller, total mechanical energy should be conserved (minus gravity exchange). The shrunk scenario uses the maximum unstable dt=0.03119 (>1/60) with very high speed ~38 m/s; semi-implicit Euler with substeps still integrates inaccurately, gaining ~137J per step (step0 6860.79 -> step1 6998.44 -> step2 7159.51 -> step4 7551.94) exceeding E0+10%+5J limit. Reducing dt to 0.005 makes integration accurate and energy conserved.
vision_note: Frames 1 to 3 show the blue body drifting slowly rightward with small displacement. In frame 4 it suddenly jumps a large distance to the right edge at the arena wall, indicating a sharp gain in speed/energy without external input.
